info.title: ThrewLines Licensing API
info.summary: Activate, validate and deactivate product licences.
info.description:
Public API for applications that ship under a ThrewLines licence.

**Authentication.** `activate` is unauthenticated: the licence key in the request body is the credential. `validate` and `deactivate` require the `activation_token` returned by `activate`, sent as a Bearer token.

**Offline verification.** Every successful call returns an `activation_token`: an ES256 JWT you verify locally against the public key published at `/.well-known/jwks.json`. Verify it offline until `check_after`, and keep working until `offline_grace_until`. That is the intended steady state - do not call the API on every launch.

**Error handling.** Branch on `code`, never on `message`. The messages are written for humans and may be reworded; the codes are stable.

**Retrying.** `RATE_LIMITED` is the only code worth retrying on its own - back off and try later. `INVALID_REQUEST` means your payload is wrong and will keep failing. Everything else is a decision about the licence itself and should be surfaced to the user. A transport failure, a non-JSON body or an HTML error page is not a licence verdict: keep the last good token and fall back to offline verification until `offline_grace_until`.

**Base path.** The server URL above already ends in `/api/license/v1`, so append only `licenses/activate` and friends. Joining a path that repeats the version, or one with a leading slash, silently produces a URL this API does not serve and you will get an HTML error page rather than a JSON failure.

host.description: The host your ThrewLines instance is served from

post.summary: Activate a licence on one installation
post.description:
Call once per installation. Returns an `activation_token` to persist and verify offline. Re-activating the same `installation_id` is idempotent and does not consume an extra activation slot.

Rate limited on two axes: 30 requests per minute per IP, and 60 per minute per licence key, so one key cannot be brute-forced from many addresses.

post.summary: Re-check an activation and refresh its token
post.description:
Call once the token's `check_after` has passed. Returns a fresh `activation_token` with new `check_after` and `offline_grace_until` values.

The `installation_id` must match the one the token was issued for. Rate limited to 120 requests per minute per IP.

post.summary: Alias for validate, for clients that poll a heartbeat
post.description:
Identical to `/licenses/validate`: same request body, same response, same rate limit, same token refresh. It exists because clients built against the previous licensing service poll this path on a timer.

New integrations should call `/licenses/validate` instead.
Frees the slot so the licence can be activated elsewhere. Call this when uninstalling or moving an installation. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute per IP.

get.summary: Public keys for verifying activation tokens
get.description: Fetch once and cache. Match the token header's `kid` to a key here, then verify the ES256 signature offline. Keys are not rotated: rotating would invalidate every licence already in the field.

200.description: A JWK Set containing the active public key.

license_key.description: The key issued to the customer. Shown once at issue time and never recoverable: only its digest is stored. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped and the key is upper-cased before matching, so case does not affect validity; the pattern describes the canonical form.

installation_id.description: A stable identifier you generate per installation, and persist. Send the same string on later validate and deactivate calls. It is hashed before storage. Activation slots are counted by this value: re-activating with an installation_id that is already active just refreshes it and consumes no extra slot, while each new value takes one until the licence reaches its activation limit. Generating a fresh value per launch will exhaust the licence.

product_code.description: The product this installation belongs to. Must match the licence or the call fails with PRODUCT_MISMATCH.

device_label.description: Human-readable label shown in the licence registry.

request_id.description: Quote this when reporting a problem; it appears in the server logs.

product_code.description: The licence's product code as stored, which is always lower-case. It may therefore differ in case from the product_code you sent. Compare case-insensitively.

entitlements.description: Whatever was recorded against the licence, for example {"seats": 3}.

activation_token.description: ES256 JWT. Persist it and verify offline.

check_after.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Call validate (or heartbeat) once this has passed. Note the token's own check_after claim is Unix seconds instead - same instant, different representation.

offline_grace_until.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Keep working offline until this, then stop. The token's grace_until claim is the same instant in Unix seconds.

code.description: Stable machine-readable reason. Branch on this.

message.description: Human-readable. May be reworded; do not parse.

kid.description: Key id. Match the token header's kid against this to choose the verifying key; a ThrewLines deployment currently publishes one key, threwlines-license-1.

TokenClaims.description: The decoded payload of an activation_token. It contains no host, domain or URL, so moving your deployment to another domain does not invalidate issued licences.

aud.description: The product code as stored, always lower-case - so a product registered as "Abedz" gives aud "abedz". Compare case-insensitively rather than against your configured value.

tv.description: Token version. Bumped to invalidate outstanding tokens for one licence.

Activation.description: The licence is active for this installation.

Failure.description: The request was refused. Branch on `code`.

example.message: This license has reached its activation limit.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Back off and retry.

example.message: Too many requests. Try again shortly.
